newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes weaker on futures fall, Oman slips.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes weaker on futures fall, Oman slips.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Tuesday in the wake of an overnight slump in global crude futures.
But differentials were mostly steady as players looked to assess the next trading month.
November Brent/Dubai was quoted at $2.08/$2.20, in 15-20 cents from London levels. December was quoted at $1.93/$2.05.
Brokers said there was interest to trade the spread despite the overnight volatility.
November Brent futures slumped $1.53 to $21.60 in London in a correction from the Iraq-related rally.
SIMEX November Brent ended 23 cents higher than London at $21.81 as players decided the sell off was overdone.
Dubai intermonth spreads were steady. November/December was assessed at 37/43, December/January at 35/42 and January/February at 35/41, little changed from the day-earlier.
October paper Tapis was quoted at $21.75/$21.95, down from $22.00/$22.30 late Monday after the Brent slide had started in London.
In the wet market, Oman woes deepened as a South Korean refiner paid 11.5 cents per barrel below MPM to a Japanese trading house for a cargo.
A major offered Oman at November's Dubai quotes plus 85 cents.
A U.S. major was said to have bought 200,000 barrels of October Minas at ICP plus eight cents. A major said Friday he had sold at plus 10 and recent deals have ranged flat to plus five.

China is said to have bought most of the one million barrels plus of October Minas to make up for lost production at Nanhai, Xijiang and Liuhua. Traders said all three fields were now back up after losing more than 260,000 barrels per day production for the last week. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo,
